newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: EXPORT INFLOWS STRENGTHEN ZIMBABWE DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: EXPORT INFLOWS STRENGTHEN ZIMBABWE DOLLAR.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed firmer on the U.S. dollar and other hard units on Tuesday on the back of export inflows of foreign currency which met with little import pressure, dealers said.

"It looks like export inflows are more on the offensive at the moment. We saw U.S.$3 million coming into the market today and there could have been more exporters coming in through other banks," one dealer commented.
He said the local unit appreciated up to 11.3650/3750 on the key U.S. dollar at one point, prompting the central Reserve Bank to intervene and siphon some of the money off the system.
The Zimbabwe dollar finally closed at 11.3700/3800 against the U.S. dollar compared with 11.3725/3825 on Monday and was at 18.9600/9900 from 19.2200/2800 versus pound sterling.
It also firmer against the mark at 6.3200/3400 compared to 6.3400/3600 and at 2.4900/5100 from 2.5000/5100 versus South Africa's rand.
